title: Why we built SkillTube
summary: Useful AI resources are scattered across repositories; SkillTube adds one free, structured place to discover them.

title: Finding a good AI skill is harder than writing one
summary: Names, descriptions, tags and activity signals help people compare projects beyond repository names.

title: Every listing lives in its own public GitHub repository
summary: Ownership, history, licence and issues stay with the developer; SkillTube provides a discovery card and link.

title: Free for developers and users, with no credit card
summary: SkillTube is designed around open-source software and free service plans, with no paid APIs or subscriptions.

title: Owners are checked against GitHub
summary: GitHub sign-in and recurring repository checks help keep listings tied to their owners.

title: Dead listings clean themselves up
summary: The catalog job checks repositories repeatedly and removes listings after consecutive failed checks.

title: AI needs data, not only skills
summary: Datasets, vector stores and databases deserve the same clear discovery as prompts and agents.

title: Small developers get a fair chance
summary: A mixed-strength search approach is intended to give useful new listings a path to discovery.

title: Badges and ticks you cannot buy
summary: SkillTube awards badges through published activity rules; audience ticks are not paid verification.

title: Reporting that is fair to both sides
summary: Reports allow a developer response, preserve reporter privacy and hide serious listings while reviewed.

title: We store as little as possible
summary: SkillTube does not store IP addresses or run analytics; country stays private and minimal records expire.

title: Why SkillTube is 18+
summary: The service requires adult users and GitHub accounts that meet the age requirement.

title: Open to the world
summary: SkillTube is a free, open-source community layer from Let's Code India for developers everywhere.

title: Open source, with the rules in public
summary: MIT-licensed code, public docs and an error-code table make the project easier to inspect.

title: Light, fast and works on a phone
summary: Native web technologies and server-rendered public pages keep the experience straightforward on small devices.

title: Start in five minutes
summary: A short path from GitHub sign-in to a tagged listing and a shareable developer channel.

title: GitHub already exists. Why SkillTube?
summary: GitHub keeps the code; SkillTube adds structured discovery, comparison and developer channels.

title: Be found by people and by AI assistants
summary: Server-rendered pages, Markdown twins, structured data and sitemaps give crawlers complete descriptions.

title: Not only skills: MCP servers, datasets, databases and AI tools
summary: Any AI-related resource in a public repository can use the same structured listing fields and tags.
